utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Case Number IT-95-12-PT, the Prosecutor versus Ivica Rajic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon and happy new year, ladies and gentlemen. For the sake of the record could I have the appearances, please. For the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon. Kenneth Scott for the Prosecution, along with Josee D'Aoust, and also Denise Gustin. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. For the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I am Zelko Olujic attorney-at-law from Croatia, and I represent Mr. Ivica Rajic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Rajic, can you hear the proceedings in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Do you have anything to complain about during your detention period?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have anything special to say about my detention. And if you will allow me, Your Honour, at the end of today's session I would like a minute to address Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll come to you at a later stage. Well, this is a Status Conference in accordance with Rule 65 bis. The purpose of this conference is to help both parties for the preparation of this case. There are several matters on the agenda. The first matter as usual is the stage of disclosure. I believe that during the last Status Conference the Prosecutor has already informed the Chamber, the Pre-Trial Judge, as well as the Defence that the state of the disclosure under Rule 66 and Rule 68 has already been completed. And as regards to the Rule 66 disclosure, all the supporting material and the written statement made by the accused and by the potential witnesses, have now been submitted to the Defence. Am I right? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I informed Mr. Harhoff in our 65 ter meeting this morning, yes, you're -- Chamber's fundamentally right. We have -- of course the supporting material was disclosed a long ago. The 66(A)(ii) witness statements have been disclosed and the vast majority - and I'll explain that in a minute - of the Rule 68 material have been disclosed. As I also explained, however, as I think Your Honour knows from your tenure at the Tribunal so far, the OTP collections are large and we do conduct various searches from time to time. And we have some weeks ago begun another project to review certain collections of materials which we should complete in the next few weeks. And I anticipate there being some -- I can't estimate a volume, I don't think it will be a huge volume, but there will be some additional material for disclosure to the Defence at that time. That is just part of our ongoing review which frankly will continue from now until judgement in the case. So that's the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And how about the Rule 68 material?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That was -- that was the Rule 68 material, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And how about the status of those translations of those materials? Is there any problem concerning the translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I don't know of any in terms of what has been produced before. I'm sure counsel will correct me if I'm wrong. I'm not aware of any. As to the new material I just brought to your attention, yes, of course, it's possible that we may find to some of it does require translation. But that's just looking ahead. I can tell the Chamber, or Your Honour, that there was another item. The Court will remember that the Chamber was good enough to -- kind enough to provide protection for three sensitive witnesses. And we had committed, according to the Court's direction, to provide summaries to the Defence of the evidence, not to disclose at this time the identities of the protected witnesses, but to provide a summary so that the Defence would at least be familiar with the substance of the anticipated evidence. And that has been provided to counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could I turn to the Defence counsel, Mr. Olujic, any comments, any remarks you would like to make on this issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Your Honour. First of all, we have to split this issue into two groups. Obviously we have received some of the material according to the rules of this Tribunal. However, as far as the summaries are concerned, as far as I understood what has been said, this has to do with what was said earlier on at 65 ter conference, and that was offered to me by my learned friend. We were also informed about the additional protection of witnesses. We don't have any objections to that at this moment. I appreciate what my learned friend is saying about the disclosure of new documents. However, I would kindly ask for the new documents to be disclosed in Croatian so that my client could have a complete insight into all of these documents and prepare for his Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, what do you mean by Croatian?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mean that all the documents that are in English should be translated into Croatian, the language that is understood and read by the accused. This is what I meant and what I had in mind was the additional documents that the Prosecutor proposes to disclose in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You are not implying there's some nuance between Serbian and Croatian, you do not mean that?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, when I say "Croatian," I am saying that my client is Croat and he speaks Croatian. However, if the documents are translated into Serbian or Bosnian, he will understand the translation. In the Republic of Croatia, the official language is Croatian; in the Republic of Serbia, the official language is Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. The rules are that the document should be translated into a language that the accused understands. Yes. Well, at this moment I have to remind the Prosecution of his obligation for the disclosure of the 68 Rule materials, which is a continuing obligation on the part of the Prosecution. And it means that whenever you have these kind of materials, you should -- are under this obligation to disclose them to the Defence. Let's turn to the next issue. The next issue is the agreed facts or the agreement on certain facts. I believe that during the last Status Conference the Prosecution is very kind to inform us that it has submitted on the 11th of August, 2004, a list of some proposed agreed facts to the Defence which is about 200 to 220. And as a Pre-Trial Judge, I appreciate this offer very much, and I believe that at that time I urged the parties to meet as soon as possible to the list. And I also requested that the parties could reach kind of agreement before this Status Conference. Could I hear that -- whether if there's any development in this aspect. Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: May it please the Court. Your Honour's memory is hundred per cent accurate. We did provide counsel with a set of proposed facts last August, and it's come up at several of our Status Conferences since then and of course again today. We of course bonded with counsel on a number of occasions, again as recently as the 11th of January this year, a few days ago, so see if progress could be made on this, for reasons that Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond I'm sure Mr. Olujic can explain to you, we don't seem to have -- been able to make any progress to date. Although we certainly are confident -- the Prosecution is confident that there should be a substantial amount of this information that can be agreed. But I am sad to report that we have not been able to make progress with the Defence to the present time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, could you be more specific. You mean that you haven't got any chance to meet with Defence on this issue, or you already met but there's no progress on this aspect?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We've had several meetings in the course of -- when these schedules -- these conferences have been scheduled and other times for other reasons Mr. Olujic has needed to be in The Hague. So we have met on a couple of occasions in which we discussed, in honesty, the topic of the proposals and the fact that progress needed to be made, but Mr. Olujic has reported to us the need at all occasions to meet with his client. And frankly, Your Honour, I'd be more comfortable for Mr. Olujic to tell you whatever difficulties he had than for me to try and interpret that for him. To answer the Chamber's questions, your questions, Your Honour, yes, we have met here in The Hague in which this topic has come up and been discussed, but we have not been able to make progress.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Olujic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. To follow-up on my learned friend's words as far as the agreed facts are concerned and the proposition sent to me by the Prosecution in the month of September, as soon as this was translated I handed it over to my client and I started with very serious work on this material. The Prosecution from its point of view included among the 200 facts proposed for agreement - and although this is not a subject of our discussion at the moment - a lot of these facts will be rejected because we will not be able to reach agreement on them. However, the Defence wants to reach an agreement in as many aspects as possible before the trial. We have come into a rather awkward position, Your Honour, me and my client, Mr. Rajic. Based on the facts, based on the material proposed by the Prosecution, my client has to re-construct certain developments and he has to try and recollect some events which took place ten years ago. In order for me to help him with the preparation of his Defence, I put certain documents on CDs. However, in communication with my client I cannot cooperate with him by handing these materials over to him because the Detention Unit wants to clear all these materials first. My client, Mr. Rajic, is strongly against that and he has bound me not to hand over any material on CD to him indirectly, that all the material has to reach him directly. Since we haven't been able to do that, I haven't been able to comply with his request because there was no goodwill on the part of the Detention Unit. That is why my client has objected on several occasions to the Detention Unit. He has also informed me that he requested a personal contact with the representatives of the registry of this Tribunal, all in order to resolve this issue which in any case slows us down in the analysis of all the materials and facts. In other words, we have been preparing our reply to the 200 proposed facts; however, we have been slowed down because the two of us cannot cooperate in the way we would like to, and that is for me to be able to hand over certain materials to him, for him to study those materials, and for the two of us to agree on the tactics, with regard to what has been proposed by the Prosecution. Unfortunately until today we have only been able to deal with only 40 or 50 per cent of the material, because everything has been slowed down. And everything now boils down to me manually processing some documents and handing them over to him. If we could do it by means of CDs, it would speed up the process which is our wish as well at the end of the day. This, Your Honour, is a problem that we face and this is I believe the reason for which Mr. Rajic wishes to address Your Honour at the end of this meeting. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Olujic, when I was informed about this CD issue in the UN Detention Unit, I made an inquiry into it. The answer I got is as follows: This is a normal procedure in the Detention Unit, and the guards in the Detention Unit is fully understanding of the privilege between the counsel and his client. They just put a mark on that CD without looking into the content of that CD. And this rule applies to everybody, every counsel, and every detainee in there. There's no discriminative intent behind it. I hope you could understand that is a purely normal safety procedure in the Detention Unit. At the same time, I also urge you to have a serious study of the proposals submitted by the Prosecution. We really believe that this proposal will greatly help both parties to identify the issue in this case, and in a great way help the positions of your client. You might divide the list into three sections. Maybe one section is just for the basic facts; the second category might be something that is in dispute, which means that you do not agree; the third section may be something you need to consider and to think it over. That will greatly facilitate the proceedings. I believe that in every case there are some basic facts which do not require the other side to produce evidence to prove it. Well, since you have not been able to finish this job, I might give you some more time to do so. I hope after this Status Conference you could carefully study the list of the proposals and have a good discussion with your client. I hope the parties could meet as soon as possible, try to reach some agreement. I have to emphasise that I'm not forcing any party to agree on some particular issues, but I still think it's a very good practice for the facilitating the proceedings of this trial. I hope before the next Status Conference we will have something concrete, which means the parties will submit to the Pre-Trial Judge a joint statement listing what are the facts that the parties have already agreed and what is still in dispute. Is that agreeable to the parties? Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it certainly is. I feel compelled to point out as counsel has indicated that Mr. Rajic needs to focus his mind on these matters in order to make some progress. And I just -- I can't imagine a person's mind not being more focused on such matters where they are the basis for him having been here in custody since June of 2003. It seems to me this would be foremost on Mr. Rajic's mind and he would be well in a position to respond to these propositions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, as the counsel said, about more or less ten years has passed. There is something that happened long ago, time for the accused to recall, it's quite understandable. Yes, Mr. Olujic, do you agree with my proposal on that issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, naturally, Your Honour, I agree with your proposal. As far as what my learned friend has just said, I don't think this is correct, and I believe that your comment is more than sufficient for me. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So before the next statement I am expecting a joint statement on what has been agreed upon by the parties and what is still in dispute. Thank you. The next issue is concerning with the preparation of this case. Mr. Scott, could you inform me somehow about where you are, for instance, whether you are going to submit 65 ter filings or whether the pre-trial brief will be prepared in the foreseeable future and whether there's any preparation for the list of the exhibits which are to be used in this trial. You may brief me on that or give me a rough idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. As I indicated to Mr. Harhoff this morning, no, that hasn't been on any recent agendas, there hasn't been any -- a specific time schedule to prepare that kind of information, so it is not something that we've looked at very recently. I've certainly -- if the Chamber wants to set a schedule for 65 ter filings, obviously we will comply with a schedule. In terms of a pre-trial brief, to be candid, Your Honour, we think it would be very premature to require a pre-trial brief the next few months. This case is not scheduled for trial and by all indications will not be scheduled for trial for some time. And frankly my personal view is it's not a particularly a good use of time or not particularly helpful to prepare these documents months and months in advance of trial. Having said that, of course, Your Honour, I'd be happy to provide the Chamber with some additional information in terms of our preparation. Of course, it's ongoing. We look at exhibits, we look at these matters. But I haven't come here this afternoon prepared to give any sort of specific figures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Is there anything that the Defence would like to say on this issue concerning with the preparation of the case?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Perhaps there was a translation error. At this point in time, given what I have just heard from the submission, I have no other proposals to make. I hear that the case is not ready for trial and that there is not even an indication of when these filings might be submitted. I hope that we will be following the Rules of Procedure and Evidence and that the Prosecution and Defence counsel will do everything to make sure that we can go to trial as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I turn to the last issue, and first of all I would like to give the floor to Mr. Rajic. Mr. Rajic, do you have something to say at this stage?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Yes, very briefly. As far as the first issue is concerned, my attorney, Mr. Olujic, has already provided sufficient explanations. I believe there is a misunderstanding here. You have mentioned the one procedure for providing material on a CD. I think that they are requesting something else in the Detention Unit, and that's the reason for this misunderstanding. I have asked the registry to deal with this issue and try to revolve the difficulties. If not, I will address you directly through my counsel. Secondly, as far as paying for my Defence is concerned, I received a decision last year stating the percentage that would be paid for my Defence. My Defence team hasn't received a single euro so far. And since I adopt my request according to the Defence strategy, I am in a position in which I can't ask people to work if they are not paid. I think that my rights are not respected in this way, and I would be grateful if you could inform me about when I will be granted the funds that are supposed to be allocated to me so that my Defence can proceed as necessary. Thank you. That's all I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Olujic, would you please confirm the second issue your client raised just now, which I mean that you haven't received a euro since the starting of the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Rajic naturally had in view the overall situation and the decision made by the registry. He's been informed that certain funds have been earmarked for his Defence and also that the registry has taken a decision that is violating his rights to a certain extent because the registry believes that he can also contribute to the expenses of his Defence and to the expenses that are as a result of investigations, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, first of all I would like to say that the fee paid to the counsel is a matter entirely within the mandate of the registrar. And if there is any complaint and disagreement with the decisions of the registrar, you could make a complaint to the registrar or you could even appeal their decisions to the President in accordance with the rules of procedure. Secondly, certainly it is the Pre-Trial Judge's duty to convey your complaint to the registrar and to see what he could do in this aspect. I believe this is all I can do at this moment, but if there are still some problems, please feel free to let me know and I'll do my best to help the Defence to solve this issue. Mr. Rajic, how about your health?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I thank you very much. And I believe that you have to take care of yourself. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: At this stage are there any other matters that the parties would like to raise? Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Only this, Mr. President: I just feel a bit compelled to respond to counsel's statements a few moments ago. The Prosecution is taking all steps to have this -- to have this case ready for trial. It's met all of its obligations in a timely way without exception. We proposed these agreed facts in August of last year, some months ago. And I can assure the Chamber and I can assure Mr. Olujic, we are taking this case seriously and we meet all our obligations fully and in a timely way, and I just do not want to be -- the suggestion be made that there is any shortcomings in our efforts to do that by counsel or the suggestion that that's the case. We are taking our obligations seriously, as we always do, and stand ready to meet with Mr. Olujic at any time, have met with him before. We stand ready to assist the Chamber in any way we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think at the very beginning I already said that we appreciate very much the efforts you have made in the preparation of this case. Now, the ball, I believe, is in the court of the Defence. And taking into consideration the specific situations in this time, I believe both parties agreed that before the next Status Conference you will submit a joint statement on this issue. This is the basis for the -- I believe in my view for the 65 ter filings, whether if certain facts have been agreed so there's no need to call that witness or we just simply take a 92 bis statement into evidence with or without cross-examination, which will greatly facilitate the proceedings. So we appreciate the efforts made by the Prosecution. Mr. Olujic, do you have some other matters to raise at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think that's all for this Status Conference. And according to the Rules, we'll hold the next Status Conference in 120 days. And as for the specific time, both parties will be informed in due time. The hearing is adjourned.
